theorem_title: The Erdos-Turan set has exactly $p$ elements
natural_language_statement:
The set $\{2pk + (k^2 \bmod p) : 0 \le k < p\}$ has exactly $p$ elements.

The defining map is injective on $\{0, \dots, p-1\}$. Since $k^2 \bmod p$ is below $p$, and $p \le 2p$, the value $2pk + (k^2 \bmod p)$ determines $k$ as its quotient by $2p$. Primality is not needed here, only $p > 0$.
source: Paul Erdos and Pal Turan, "On a problem of Sidon in additive number theory, and on some related problems", J. London Math. Soc. 16 (1941) 212-215
